title: 对亚洲母亲无所不能的刻板印象(3)
desc: 对亚洲母亲无所不能的刻板印象(3)

paragraphs.en: It was up to our mothers to enforce these principles.
paragraphs.zh: 母亲的职责就是监督我们遵守这些准则。

paragraphs.en: Most of us grew up in households in which men earned the money, while women were tasked with the childcare – and "care" was often understood to mean preparing us for battle in a brutally competitive world.
paragraphs.zh: 我们大多数人成长的家庭里，男人负责赚钱，女性承担育儿，而这里所说的“照料”，往往意味着把我们训练好，在残酷竞争的世界里奔赴战场。

paragraphs.en: Excellence was demanded, but support was not always forthcoming.
paragraphs.zh: 家人要求我们做到优秀，却未必总能给予支持。

paragraphs.en: "She never helped me in anything academic," Min said of her mother, "but she expected that I'd get a Princeton acceptance letter."
paragraphs.zh: 敏谈起母亲：“学业上她从来不会帮我，但她期待我拿到普林斯顿大学录取通知书。”

paragraphs.en: These high expectations came at a cost.
paragraphs.zh: 这些高期待，是要付出代价的。

paragraphs.en: "She thought she had to be strict to ensure that we had the best education, because that would set us up better in later life," said another friend, Lea, of her mother.
paragraphs.zh: 另一位朋友莉娅谈及她的母亲：“她认为必须严格要求，才能保证我们获得最好的教育，让我们未来过得更好。”

paragraphs.en: That came with a "lack of recognition" that that kind of strictness "would really just damage my sense of self-worth".
paragraphs.zh: 可母亲没有意识到，这种严苛，“只会摧毁我的自我价值感”。

paragraphs.en: The fraught intimacy that develops between mother and child has a way of curdling into hatred.
paragraphs.zh: 母女之间这种紧绷又亲密的关系，有时会变质，滋生怨恨。

paragraphs.en: "My mum and I are quite similar," Lea recalled.
paragraphs.zh: 莉娅回忆：“我妈妈和我性格很像。

paragraphs.en: "So we would clash a lot growing up, because we would bring out the absolute worst in each other. We still do."
paragraphs.zh: 所以成长过程中我们频繁冲突，因为我们总能激发出彼此最坏的一面。到现在依旧如此。”

paragraphs.en: In Severance, Ma portrays the home as the site of an unhappy battle of wills.
paragraphs.zh: 马凌在《幸福蒙太奇》中将家描绘成一场意志之间不愉快的拉锯战场。

paragraphs.en: The narrator recalls, of her mother: "She was the one to punish me, sending me to kneel in the bathtub of the darkened bathroom, carrying my father's Casio watch with an alarm setting to account for when the time was up."
paragraphs.zh: 书中叙述者回忆母亲：“惩罚我的人是她，让我跪在漆黑浴室的浴缸里，她带着父亲那台设有闹钟的卡西欧手表，计时，到点才结束。”

paragraphs.en: The narrator continues: "It was I who would kneel for even longer, going further and further, taking more punishment just to spite her."
paragraphs.zh: 叙述者继续写道：“而我会主动跪更久，不断加码，承受更多惩罚，只为和她赌气。”

paragraphs.en: The effects of this kind of parenting on children have been often discussed: the pain, the lingering feelings of inadequacy, the longing for what could have been.
paragraphs.zh: 这种教养方式带给孩子的影响常被讨论：伤痛、挥之不去的自我否定、对另一种人生的向往。

paragraphs.en: After all, it is usually the children who write the books and the films about this experience.
paragraphs.zh: 毕竟，写下这些故事、拍成电影的，往往是子女一代。

paragraphs.en: But how is it seen by the mothers themselves?
paragraphs.zh: 但母亲自己又是如何看待这一切？

paragraphs.en: (An early vision of this article sought to interview my friends' mothers, but this unravelled after interviews with friends established the many secrets they were still keeping from their parents.)
paragraphs.zh: （本文最初计划采访朋友们的母亲，但在和朋友们交谈后，发现她们还有许多秘密瞒着父母，采访计划最终作罢。）

paragraphs.en: When I asked my friends about the backgrounds of their mothers, there were a wide range of answers, but plenty of shared experiences.
paragraphs.zh: 当我向朋友们询问她们母亲的成长背景，答案各不相同，却有许多共通经历。

paragraphs.en: Most grew up at a time of great instability and poverty, and they, too, did not receive much warmth from their parents.
paragraphs.zh: 她们大多成长在动荡、贫困的年代，自己年少时，也很少从父母那里得到温情。

paragraphs.en: "I'm not sure if my mum can recall a single instance of her mother doing something good to her as a child," said Lea.
paragraphs.zh: 莉娅说：“我不确定我妈妈能不能想起一件小时候她母亲善待她的事。”

paragraphs.en: Min's mother grew up in a "deeply misogynist" upper-class family in mainland China.
paragraphs.zh: 敏的母亲在中国大陆一个极度重男轻女的上层家庭长大。

paragraphs.en: As the eldest daughter in the family, she was called to care for her siblings, particularly her younger brother, who was the golden boy of the family.
paragraphs.zh: 作为家里的长女，她要照顾弟弟妹妹，尤其是家中宝贝小儿子。

paragraphs.en: By her mid-20s, she was married to a stranger approved by her father.
paragraphs.zh: 二十五岁左右，她嫁给父亲选定的陌生人。

paragraphs.en: An emotion that emerged in many of these accounts was anger: anger at missed life opportunities; anger at being expected to be mothers to their brothers; anger at being denied a divorce because it would look bad to the rest of the family.
paragraphs.zh: 许多叙述里反复出现一种情绪：愤怒。为错失的人生机遇愤怒；为被要求像母亲一样照料弟弟而愤怒；为无法离婚、怕家族蒙羞而愤怒。

paragraphs.en: This anger – usually unarticulated, given Confucian family ideals and traditional gender expectations – often ricocheted on to the person immediately around to receive it: the child.
paragraphs.zh: 受儒家家庭观念和传统性别期待束缚，这份愤怒通常不会说出口，却常常转嫁到身边最亲近的人身上——也就是孩子。

paragraphs.en: Min's mother "has a real resentment for her life", she told me.
paragraphs.zh: 敏告诉我，她母亲“对自己的人生满怀怨怼。”

paragraphs.en: "She went from her parents' house to my dad's house and that's it.
paragraphs.zh: “她从原生家庭直接嫁去我父亲家，人生仅此而已。

paragraphs.en: I don't think she made any real choices in her life.
paragraphs.zh: 我觉得她这辈子没有真正为自己做过选择。

paragraphs.en: She would yell and be abusive (to her kids).
paragraphs.zh: 她会大吼大叫，苛责孩子。

paragraphs.en: I think she did it to make herself feel better: if she's making you feel bad, then you would understand."
paragraphs.zh: 我想她这么做，是为了让自己好受一点：当她让你痛苦时，你就能体会她的感受。”

paragraphs.en: Several of my friends' parents are haunted by missed opportunities – some were unable to go to university, as they grew up during China's Cultural Revolution.
paragraphs.zh: 我几位朋友的父母都被错失的机会所困扰——有些人成长于文革时期，没能上大学。

paragraphs.en: (Severance concludes with the narrator recalling a time her mother wistfully imagined a different life for herself, one in which she had a career.)
paragraphs.zh: （《幸福蒙太奇》结尾，叙述者回忆母亲曾怅然想象另一种人生，一份属于她自己的事业。）

paragraphs.en: These feelings of loss and missed opportunities stand at odds with the larger story of 20th-century east Asia, which is often spoken of in tones of triumph: about how nations such as China, Singapore and South Korea transformed from war-torn rural backwaters to become homes to gleaming megacities.
paragraphs.zh: 这种失落感与人生遗憾，和20世纪东亚宏大叙事形成反差。人们提起这段历史，总带着胜利口吻：中国、新加坡、韩国等国家，如何从饱经战火的乡村穷地，崛起为矗立着璀璨大都市的地方。

paragraphs.en: But it has more often been men who have been encouraged to walk boldly into this shiny new world.
paragraphs.zh: 但往往是男性，被鼓励大胆踏入这个崭新光鲜的世界。

paragraphs.en: In reality, as in fiction, the mothers are left to navigate the space between the past and future.
paragraphs.zh: 现实如同小说描绘的那样，母亲们只能徘徊在过去与未来之间。
